title: Otis Ferguson and Edward Nichols in Jazzmen
summary: Perhonas asks about Ferguson's New Republic pieces on Bix and who wrote the Bix chapter.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: Okay. See, before we get off the subject of Jasmine, I wanted to ask just about a few more people in here. I'm especially interested in, well, to a certain extent, at least, in Otis Ferguson, because Otis Ferguson wrote several articles in the 30s in...
I have three or four of them in the original.
Right, in which he sets... He's talking about Big Spiderbeck, and the title of the article is Young Man with a Horn.

And it seems to me what he did in those articles was create the jazz musician as a kind of romantic artist for the first time. Well, maybe not the first time, but for a national audience. Yeah, I noticed that. I noticed he had an article, he had a chapter in the book, Jasmine, on... Not on Bix, because another person did that. Let's see.
Can you look it up in the table of contents?
Yeah, I ought to just look it up in the table of contents.
I don't think I ever did meet him.

Oh, Red Nichols. Now, this to me is very interesting, because if Otis Ferguson was interested in Bix, why didn't he write the chapter on Bix? But that's... Let's see. Who wrote the chapter on Bix? Edwards. Edward J. Nichols. Nichols. Who I don't know who he...
Nichols writes the Bix chapter and...
Yeah. He's not related to Red Nichols, no. No. No, no. You don't know anything about either Ferguson or Nichols?

Nichols is some teacher. I think at a Pennsylvania college, like maybe Penn State or something like that. I don't know what he taught. I think he was. And I never did meet Ferguson, I'm sorry, because he must have been quite a nice guy and an important writer. A good writer. He was a good writer. An early jazz writer, yeah. He was a good writer. He died very early. I guess soon after this book came out, probably.
